name: Columbus Museum of Art
notes: The Columbus Museum of Art, from published descriptions (the museum, Zahner, copper.org) and the ground file's footprint (about 90 x 70 m, square to the street grid, East Broad Street on the north): the 1931 Renaissance Revival building by Richards, McCarty & Bulford, a long symmetrical stone front with a base course, three arched portals in the central frontispiece, end pavilions and cornice, galleries round the glass-roofed Derby Court; the Margaret M. Walter Wing (DesignGroup, 2015) to the east, clad in pre-patinated copper (drawn in the dark brown) with glazed north and south fronts and a gallery reaching out over the entrance; the sculpture garden. Guessed: heights, the wing's exact size and cantilever, the court's size, stone colour. No photographs were available.
